summary: X_ITE is a JavaScript viewer that runs inside a web page and draws three-dimensional scenes in the browser using WebGL. Its native format is X3D, which it reads in XML, JSON and Classic VRML encodings, and it also loads VRML, glTF, VRM, OBJ, STL and PLY files by converting them to X3D internally. It covers scene structure, event routing, scripting in ECMAScript, physically based materials, shadows, sound, humanoid animation, geospatial placement, rigid body physics, particles, volume data and, experimentally, Gaussian splats, and it has basic WebXR support for headsets. It leaves identity, payment, multi-user networking, content moderation and world persistence to other systems, and the X3D nodes for networked simulation are marked as not supported. A trap for a standards audience: X_ITE implements most but not all of X3D (the supported-nodes page counts 246 of 259 nodes), and it adds its own nodes and experimental X3D 4.1 features, so support for a node should be checked against its page rather than assumed from the profile.
